s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
key_facts: Previous treatments included systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
key_facts: Previous treatments included systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical examination revealed violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, and erythematous papules, consistent with dermatomyositis. Elevated serum IFN-β levels and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies also support this diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Photosensitive eruption, systemic symptoms, and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies are consistent with lupus erythematosus. However, the lack of specific serologic results and other characteristic lupus features makes this diagnosis less likely than dermatomyositis.

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlapping features of dermatomyositis, lupus erythematosus, and other autoimmune diseases are present, making mixed connective tissue disease a possible diagnosis. However, the clinical presentation is more consistent with dermatomyositis.

shortlist.label: Poikiloderma with neutropenia
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse poikiloderma is a characteristic feature of this disease, but the lack of reported neutropenia and other specific features makes this diagnosis less likely.

shortlist.label: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and systemic symptoms could be consistent with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, but the presence of photosensitive eruption, poikiloderma, and specific autoantibodies makes dermatomyositis a more likely diagnosis.

raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, erythematous flat-topped papules, dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and radiographic evidence of myositis, along with elevated serum IFN-β levels and anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, are characteristic findings of dermatomyositis, especially in the context of a 6-year history of photosensitive eruption and minimal improvement with various treatments.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While lupus can present with similar skin findings and autoantibodies, the specific combination of poikiloderma, Gottron's papules (flat-topped papules on extensor joints), and myositis points more strongly towards dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: This condition often presents with a combination of features from lupus, scleroderma, and polymyositis/dermatomyositis, but the prominent dermatomyositis features in this case make it a less likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Poikiloderma with neutropenia
rejected.why: This rare condition is characterized by poikiloderma and neutropenia, but the presence of myositis, specific autoantibodies, and the pattern of skin involvement suggest dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis
rejected.why: While this condition can present with skin manifestations and autoantibodies, the specific pattern of skin involvement, muscle findings, and autoantibody profile in this case are more consistent with dermatomyositis.
